chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed altogether, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abdul-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Three (people) Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept their prayer; one of them is the absconding slave until he returns to his master.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الْآبِقُ: The absconding slave who flees his master's authority

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people whose prayers Allah does not accept according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS), identifying the 'absconding slave' (al-abd al-abiq) as the first of three categories whose prayers are rejected until they return to their master. This highlights the principle that specific forms of disobedience or rebellion can invalidate the spiritual efficacy of worship, serving as a metaphor for the soul's servitude to God.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Al Husayn Bin Saeed altogether, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Abdul Hameed, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Three (people) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic will not Accept their Prayers – one of them is the absconding slave until he returns to his master’.
